proof.text: The jointly surjective etale family generates a covering sieve S on T: etale maps are flat and locally of finite presentation. For each Z over T, pull S back along Z to T and transport it to Over T via Sieve.overEquiv. This gives a covering sieve R(Z). Every arrow W to Z in R(Z) supplies a factorization of W to T through some T_i. Pullback covering stability is the sieve form of the base-change covering assertion [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change].

proof.text: The pullback U_i to T_i is an open immersion, hence a monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. Thus Hom over T_i from any W to U_i is a subsingleton. The local representing isomorphism makes F(W) a subsingleton whenever W to T factors through T_i. Applying separatedness from [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] on R(Z) shows that F(Z) is a subsingleton for every Z. Transport between equal structural maps uses the identity isomorphism of their underlying schemes.

proof.text: For each arrow W to U in R(U), choose a factorization W to T_i to T. The maps W to U and W to T_i give a map W to U_i by [def-pc-fibre-product], and alpha_i produces a section on W. Every section type is a subsingleton by step 2, so this family is compatible. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] glues it to a section b of F(U). This construction also applies to the empty covering.

source.place: Tag 041X, lemma-descending-property-open-immersion, the morphism obtained by gluing; explicit natural-transformation and restriction calculation for the sheaf version.

proof.text: For a section x in F(Z) and any point z of Z, choose a point t_i above its image in T. There is a point p of Z times_T T_i above z and t_i: this is the pointwise joint-surjectivity assertion in [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], implemented by Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback. Restrict x to this pullback and apply the inverse local representing isomorphism to obtain a map to U_i. Composing with U_i to U and evaluating at p shows that the image of z lies in U. Therefore the image of Z to T is contained in U. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to obtain a map Z to U over T.

proof.text: Use the universe-lifted Yoneda equivalence to define eta from h_U to F by a mapping to its pullback of b. Each component is injective because maps to an open are a subsingleton by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. It is surjective because any section provides a map to U by step 4, and all sections agree by step 2. The componentwise bijections give a natural isomorphism alpha.

proof.text: The prescribed local restrictions and the section formula hold because their two sides lie in the same subsingleton section type. Any competing natural isomorphism agrees componentwise for the same reason, so equals alpha. The factorization of step 4 is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], and its pullback section equals x by subsingletonness. If there is a map to U, pulling back b supplies a section, while step 4 rules out sections when no such map exists. No finiteness, reducedness or nonemptiness assumption was used.

title: Representation of an fppf sheaf by a prescribed etale-locally representing open
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], within the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\{q_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $U\subseteq T$ be a specified open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $U_i=U\times_TT_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $i$, suppose given a natural isomorphism $\alpha_i:h_{U_i/T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_{T_i}$ of presheaves on $\mathit{Sch}/T_i$, where $h_{U_i/T_i}(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_{T_i}(Z,U_i)$ and $F|_{T_i}(Z\to T_i)=F(Z\to T_i\to T)$. There exists a unique natural isomorphism $\alpha:h_{U/T}\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, where $h_{U/T}(Z)=\operatorname{Mor}_T(Z,U)$, whose restriction to every $T_i$ is $\alpha_i$ under the fibre-product identification. If $b=\alpha_U(\operatorname{id}_U)\in F(U)$, its component on any $g:Z\to T$ sends $v:Z\to U$ over $T$ to $v^*b$. Every $x\in F(Z)$ determines a unique factorization $v:Z\to U$ of $g$, and $x=v^*b$; consequently $F(Z)$ is a singleton when $g$ factors through $U$ and is empty otherwise. No compatibility hypothesis on the local isomorphisms, finiteness of $I$, quasi-compactness of the schemes, or algebraic-space hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.
